source.title: Learning to See Before Seeing: Demystifying LLM Visual Priors from Language Pre-training
source.authors: Junlin Han; Shengbang Tong; David Fan; Yufan Ren; Koustuv Sinha; P. Torr; Filippos Kokkinos

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream multimodal performance across model and pre-training data scales, a different measure from the loss-scaling claims.
record.gate_note: The study measures VQA accuracy across model sizes and pre-training token volumes, not held-out cross-entropy loss or power-law fits. Its references to prior scaling-law work are citations, not results from those studies. Figure 1 reports the relevant scale sweeps; the paper gives qualitative descriptions rather than exact plotted values.
record.test_reason: Section 3.1 trains five Llama-3-style LLMs (340M–13B) on 0–100B web-crawl tokens, adapts each into an MLLM, and reports downstream VQA accuracy against model and data scale. This is a new setting (downstream multimodal tasks after visual adaptation) with a result bearing on V6. No power laws are fitted, so only the direction and uniformity of scaling are tested, not its predictability. T3 fits better than T2 because the question is the downstream-scaling claim in a new modality and pipeline.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase covers only Section 3.1. The paper's main conclusion is that LLM visual priors decompose into a reasoning prior and a perception prior. The reasoning prior is driven by reasoning-centric text (code, math, academia), scales with its proportion, and transfers across vision encoders. The perception prior emerges diffusely from broad data and depends more on the vision encoder and instruction tuning. Visual-description text saturates quickly. A reasoning-heavy balanced mixture improves VQA at 7B/1T without hurting language ability. The scale finding (VQA scales positively but non-uniformly) is one secondary result.
record.recipe_differences: Measures downstream multimodal VQA accuracy across model sizes and data volumes; does not fit power laws to held-out pre-training loss or study compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling pattern varies by VQA category and, for Vision-Centric VQA, by model size.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed scale (3B, 30B tokens), the proportion of reasoning-centric data raises VQA accuracy progressively up to 75%. Visual-description data saturates quickly (Figure 3, Table 1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream multimodal performance depends on pre-training data composition in ways not captured by scale alone.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR), as stated in the supplied record
record.problems: Figure 1 is the source for the scale-sweep results; exact plotted values and uncertainty estimates are not reported in the text. The evaluations concern downstream visual accuracy, not held-out language-model loss.
record.rows_left_out: No additional Figure 1 category results left out; rows summarize the reported category-level trends rather than extracting individual plotted points.

untested.parts: Quantitative predictability: no fitted scaling relation and no extrapolation. No direct test of downstream accuracy as a function of pre-training loss across scale (Figure 1 reports no loss or perplexity).
Not tested: no loss is reported against parameters or tokens.
Not tested: the multimodal adaptation results have no power-law fit.

missing.what: Perplexity (Wikitext/LAMBADA) and VQA accuracy across 11 data mixtures at fixed 3B/50B. Perplexity worsens slightly while VQA improves, decoupling loss from downstream accuracy.
7B/1T-token comparison: the Balanced mix has lower perplexity (7.49 vs 8.72) and higher overall VQA (38.64 vs 37.32) than the language-favorable mix.

record.verdict_notes: Scale is a minor part of this paper, which focuses on data composition. All scale evidence is figure-only, with no tabulated values or uncertainty, and comes from a single seed. The test is of downstream accuracy after a two-stage MLLM adaptation, so the scale effect is mediated by adaptation. Perplexity here is measured on Wikitext/LAMBADA, not on held-out pre-training data.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pre-training loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations at fixed compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Whether power-law forms hold across modalities or training regimes; the study evaluates visual-task accuracy but does not test a power-law form.
The study evaluates downstream VQA accuracy across model and data scales, but does not test predictability from pre-training loss or fit a quantitative scaling relation.
Dependence of fitted loss exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Avg, General and Knowledge VQA, 340M–13B models, 0–100B web-crawl tokens
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises with both model size and data volume (r1–r3). The improvement is shown directionally, not as a fitted law.
relationships.display_finding: Average, General and Knowledge VQA accuracy increased with both model size and pretraining-data volume.

relationships.reason: OCR & Chart barely responds to data volume, and Vision-Centric plateaus early for small models, so scaling is not uniform across task categories (r4, r5).
relationships.display_finding: OCR and chart performance barely responded to data volume, while vision-centric performance plateaued early for small models.

relationships.condition: Across pre-training data mixtures at fixed scale (3B, 50B tokens; Table 2)
relationships.reason: This verdict is based on the text (Table 2), not on any row. Across mixtures, Wikitext/LAMBADA perplexity worsens slightly (13.46→13.88) while VQA accuracy rises (32.4→33.4). So downstream VQA is not tracked by language-model loss when data composition changes.
relationships.display_finding: Changing data mixtures worsened perplexity from 13.46 to 13.88 while raising VQA accuracy from 32.4 to 33.4.
